verdict.rationale: MotherDuck docs describe several least-privilege mechanisms usable for agents: restricting the MCP server to read-only access vs. the newer read-write query_rw tool, 'SaaS Mode' to limit local environment interaction, and per-account-scoped secrets not shared across the org. This covers the core intent of scoped agent credentials but stops short of fine-grained per-resource or time-boxed token scoping. Missing for 10: granular table/database-level credential scoping specifically for agent tokens, token expiration/rotation controls, and independent verification that read-only restriction is enforced robustly.
